title: Recurrence relation
summary: A relation constraining indexed values using other indexed values, often earlier ones.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

assumptions.text: A sequence or family of indexed values is specified.

content.plain: A recurrence describes how values are linked across index steps. It need not always determine a unique sequence unless enough initial data and uniqueness conditions are supplied.
content.exact: A recurrence relation for a sequence (a_n) is a relation R(n,a_n,a_{n-1},...,a_{n-k}) that is required to hold for specified n. A recurrence plus initial conditions may determine the sequence.
content.caveat: A recurrence alone implies neither periodicity nor chaos; the state space, update rule, initial data, and mode of iteration must be declared.

relations.note: Some recurrences admit alternative explicit formula representations.

verification.method: Revision migration checked for exact-reference closure and editorial mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.
